subject: Frostline: Confidence restoration plan and action trace
messages:
From: Hannah Lowe <hannah.lowe@frostline.io>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Miguel Santos <miguel.santos@frostline.io>, support@frostline.io
Date: Sun, 05 Dec 2027 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Production surge — site-wide latencies (Dec 4)

Hi Sofia,

We saw a sustained latency spike across our checkout flows yesterday evening (Dec 4) starting ~22:30 PST.  p95 jumped from 250ms to 2.1s and error-rate on the generation endpoint rose to ~4.5% for a 40-minute window. This caused a drop in completed checkouts and triggered our fallback to minimal-recommendation mode.

Can your team share an initial post-incident summary and whether there are immediate mitigations we should keep in place? Our ops manager (Miguel) is on standby.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Lowe
Head of Platform Reliability | Frostline Retail
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Lowe <hannah.lowe@frostline.io>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Miguel Santos <miguel.santos@frostline.io>
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2027 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production surge — site-wide latencies (Dec 4)

Hi Hannah — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the impact. Short recap:

- Root cause (initial): sudden increase in very long prompt requests from a 3rd-party recommendation job that bypassed our prefix cache and blocked slots on a shard serving Frostline traffic.
- Immediate mitigation we enacted: throttled internal recommendation job, bumped dedicated pool size for your tenant, and enabled short-circuit caching for common prompt prefixes used by checkout.
- Observable impact after mitigations: p95 reduced to 330ms within 9 minutes; error rate returned to baseline after autoscale warmed.

We're drafting a formal RCA and a corrective-action plan (including runbook updates and a short-term QoS routing change). I propose a leadership sync tomorrow at 10am PST to walk through the RCA and attach the action tracker.

Action items pending from us: full RCA doc + action tracker (EOD Dec 8), and a proposed canary for the routing change (Dec 10).

I'll attach the working RCA and a tracker once they're ready.

—Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Customer Reliability Lead | Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Lowe <hannah.lowe@frostline.io>, Miguel Santos <miguel.santos@frostline.io>
Date: Wed, 08 Dec 2027 10:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production surge — site-wide latencies (Dec 4)

FYI attaching the first-pass RCA and the tracker (see attachments). Key points for the exec sync:

1) Timeline of events (exact traces + autoscale timings)
2) Short-term controls: prefix cache hardening, per-tenant admission limits, and increased warm pool headroom
3) Medium-term: QoS routing policy change + model-variant fallback for heavy prompt lengths
4) Long-term: instrumentation changes to surface prompt-length heatmaps and per-route cost SLOs

I recommend we commit to the canary on Dec 10 (low traffic window), with an on-call runbook for rollback within 5 minutes.

-David
From: Hannah Lowe <hannah.lowe@frostline.io>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Miguel Santos <miguel.santos@frostline.io>
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2027 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production surge — site-wide latencies (Dec 4)

Thanks David & Sofia — we reviewed the doc internally. A couple of asks before the exec sync:

- Can you add the exact KV-cache miss rate for the spike window (we need that to confirm our mitigation made a material difference)?
- Please include a short note on whether your billing or chargeback will be impacted by the temporary bump in dedicated capacity (we need to brief our CFO).

We'll plan to attend the canary on Dec 10 and will have a rep in the war room.

Hannah
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Lowe <hannah.lowe@frostline.io>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Miguel Santos <miguel.santos@frostline.io>
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2027 07:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production surge — site-wide latencies (Dec 4)

Hannah — attach is an update with the cache-miss metrics and a short finance note. Summary:

- KV cache miss rate during the 22:30-23:10 window: 78% (vs baseline 18%). That aligns with the overload behavior we saw.
- Cost impact: 6-hour elevated dedicated footprint; estimated incremental chargeback = $1,200 (we'll invoice per our reserved capacity pass-through policy).

Canary plan (today Dec 10, 23:00 PST):
- Step 0: Snapshot current routing config (Marissa)
- Step 1: Enable per-tenant admission limiter for heavy prompts (Karthik)
- Step 2: Turn on prefix short-circuit cache for checkout routes (Sofia)
- Step 3: Monitor p95 / error-rate / 1-min average CPU on shard nodes (David)
- Rollback: revert routing and admission limiter if p95 increases >20% from baseline for 5 consecutive minutes

We'll be in the war room; Miguel, Hannah — thanks for joining.

Attachments: corrective-actions-tracker.xlsx

-Marissa
From: Miguel Santos <miguel.santos@frostline.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Lowe <hannah.lowe@frostline.io>
Date: Sun, 12 Dec 2027 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production surge — site-wide latencies (Dec 4) — post-canary notes

Quick update from Frostline side after the canary (Dec 10):

- Canary result: passed. Checkout p95 remained within +12% of baseline; error-rate stayed below 0.6% during the window.
- Outstanding ask: we want a firm schedule for the medium-term QoS routing rollout and the instrumentation changes (prompt-length heatmaps). We need dates to include in our internal postmortem.

From our side we appreciated the quick rollback mechanism and the cost transparency. Please confirm target dates for the medium-term items and the owner for the runbook update so I can close our internal ticket.

-Miguel

On Fri, Dec 10, 2027 at 23:10 Redwood War Room wrote:
> Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com> wrote:
> > Canary completed. No regressions observed. Rolling to monitoring.
> > —Sofia
>
> War Room Log: prefix cache set, admission limiter active, 23:00-23:20 PST. No adverse signals.
